meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law statutory company law foundation with indigenous Samoan customary law overlay)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 6-7 (name), s. 9 (registered office and registered agent), ss. 17A-17D (beneficial ownership records; Amendment Act 2008 abolishing bearer shares); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007 (as amended by the AML/CFT Amendment Act 2019), Parts on customer due diligence and beneficial ownership; Samoa International Financial Authority Act 2012; Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Rules and Financial Institutions AML/CFT Directive 2021; Foreign Investment Act 2000 (for any physical manufacturing business in Samoa).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Name Reservation / Name Approval
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of International Companies through the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) authentication followed by Consular Legalization at the consulate/high commission of the destination jurisdiction (Samoa is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certified True Copy of passport and proof of residential address for each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the UBO's/director's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin state is a contracting party (e.g., China, Hong Kong, Singapore); otherwise Consular Legalization at the nearest Samoa diplomatic/consular post or at the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Apia

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Bank Reference Letter and Source of Wealth declaration for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Retaining bank (ABA/SWIFT member) and the UBO, jointly notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (origin in Hague contracting state) or Consular Legalization at the Samoa Embassy/High Commission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed UBO Declaration and Beneficial Ownership Register form (ROBO register entry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Registered Agent / Corporate Service Provider in Samoa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of signature page in the UBO's jurisdiction plus MFAT authentication and Consular Legalization if the document is presented outside Samoa for banking or regulatory purposes

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Agent Consent and Registered Office Acceptance Letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No foreign legalization required for domestic filing; if used for foreign bank/fintech onboarding (Stripe/PingPong), requires MFAT authentication and Consular Legalization of the destination state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, Register of Directors and Register of Members (Certified Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: MFAT authentication and Consular Legalization by the jurisdiction where the banking/regulatory counterparty is located (no Apostille available in Samoa)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT Sanctions List, Australian DFAT Consolidated List, and the domestic list maintained by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit. PEP rule: any politically exposed person (PEP) is subject to enhanced due diligence (EDD) requiring board-level approval of the Registered Agent's Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO), verification of source of wealth and source of funds, and 90-day periodic review. Adverse media and high-risk jurisdiction (FATF/APG) negative news checks are mandatory. Failure of any screen is a disqualifying event for incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) International Companies Registry - Name Approval and Reservation System (lodged exclusively through a licensed Samoa Registered Agent; no direct public self-service portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official register is maintained in English. The registered corporate name must be in Latin (roman) script. A Chinese-character trade name may be adopted by shareholders' resolution and recorded as a 'dual name' in the articles, but only the Latin-script name has statutory effect in Samoa. The memorandum and articles may be bilingual (English and Chinese) with the English text prevailing in any conflict; for Chinese family-trust structures, the Chinese dual name is endorsed on the certificate for bank and escrow recognition only.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Trustee', 'Insurance', 'Assurance', 'Reinsurance', 'Building Society', 'Finance' (when implying a licensed deposit-taking or insurance business)
'Chamber of Commerce', 'University', 'Polytechnic', 'Institute' (when implying academic or professional statutory status)
'Government', 'Ministry', 'Authority', 'National' (implying sovereign, Crown or Samoa Government connection without the written consent of the relevant Minister)
Any name identical or 'so nearly resembling' an existing registered company, trade mark or business name as to be likely to deceive (ICA 1987, s. 6)
'Group', 'Holdings', 'International' (permissible only when the entity factually meets group/holding structure or cross-border business substance)
Misuse of 'Limited' or approved abbreviations; the permitted suffix is 'Limited' or its abbreviation 'Ltd.'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are renewable for one additional period of 90 days by filing a renewal request with the Registrar through the Registered Agent prior to expiry. On rejection, the Registered Agent may within 14 days submit a written Administrative Review Application to the Registrar of International Companies identifying the statutory basis for permissibility (ICA 1987, s. 6(2)) and the distinguishing features of the proposed name; the Registrar issues a written determination within 14 business days. If the Administrative Review is denied, a fresh reservation may be filed using a different distinctive element; no statutory administrative appellate tribunal exists, and further recourse is by judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted in the offshore-vehicle sense. The Samoa International Company must at all times maintain a registered office at the business address of its licensed Registered Agent in Samoa (ICA 1987, s. 9), which serves as the statutory domicile and service address; no physical operational premises in Samoa are required for a non-resident IP-holding and contract-manufacturing vehicle. A virtual correspondence address in the destination market (e.g., Hong Kong SAR or Singapore) is permissible for commercial and payment-rail purposes, but the target payment rails (Stripe, platform credit cards) require the IC to maintain a physical business address and returns/operating address in the jurisdiction where the aligner products are sold or warehoused; such address is separate from the Samoa registered office and must be established in the operating jurisdiction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 10-15% annual probability of a SIFA/Central Bank of Samoa examination of the Registered Agent's client file and UBO register; direct unannounced physical inspection of the International Company's own premises is materially zero because the IC has no operational premises in Samoa (statutory substance is located at the Registered Agent's office). FATF/APG enhanced follow-up reporting on Samoa may temporarily increase document-level inspection intensity for high-risk or high-volume entities; a manufacturing license under the Foreign Investment Act 2000 and a Business License under the Business Licenses Act 1998 would only be triggered if actual physical manufacturing is carried on in Samoa, which is not contemplated for this offshore structure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 of Samoa, as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2015, ss. 6–10, 18, 28, 31, 44 and 52
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form 1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company) and Form 4 (Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Company must issue at least one share with par value of USD 1.00. No escrow account or paid-up capital deposit requirement applies to a Samoa International Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the subscribers to the incorporation application hereby resolve: (1) that the Company is incorporated as an International Company under the International Companies Act 1987; (2) that the subscription of one ordinary share at a par value of USD 1.00 be and is accepted and the directors are authorized to issue the share certificate; (3) that the registered office of the Company be fixed at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa; (4) that the proposed director and secretary, as named in the Statement of Particulars, be and are hereby appointed to hold office from the date of incorporation; and (5) that the directors and secretary be authorized to execute and file all documents necessary to perfect the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Office, MCIL, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation request via the Companies Office online portal or in person. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Samoa company, and must end with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Société Anonyme' or an approved abbreviation. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain a Certificate of Reservation.
required_dossiers: Name Search Request Form
Proposed constitutional name (English only or bilingual with a recognised abbreviation)
Proof of identity of the applicant or authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or objection, the applicant may: (a) submit an alternative name for expedited re-search; or (b) appeal in writing to the Registrar under the International Companies Act 1987 for an administrative review within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarisation of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent in Samoa and Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the Statement of Particulars (Form 3), and the Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent (Form 4). The subscriber(s) must sign each page before a Notary Public or, where the subscriber is a corporate entity, the authorised officer must sign under a board resolution and affix the corporate seal. All documents must be in English; if any translation is used, the English text prevails.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Form 3 – Statement of Particulars (directors, secretary, shareholders and registered agent)
Form 4 – Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent
Notarised consent of proposed directors and secretary
Subscriber identification documents (certified true copies of passports or national ID)
If corporate subscriber: certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing and board resolution appointing the authorised signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any notarial certificate or statement of good standing, the registered agent may cure by obtaining a legalised apostille from the competent authority of the issuing jurisdiction or by resubmitting corrected forms within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Office, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed and notarised constitutional documents, together with Forms 1, 3 and 4, at the Companies Office counter or through the online filing platform. Pay the official filing fee and any stamp duty. The Registrar will examine the documents for statutory compliance, verify the registered agent is licensed, and if satisfied, issue the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation
Form 3 – Statement of Particulars
Form 4 – Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent
Memorandum and Articles of Association (notarised)
Filing fee payment receipt
Proof of registered agent's licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, the registered agent must submit a written cure notice and corrected filing within 14 days. If the application is rejected, the full filing fee (except name reservation fee) is applied to a resubmitted application within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and establishment of statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Office, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and date of incorporation. The registered agent then prepares the statutory registers, including the register of members, register of directors, register of secretaries, register of charges and the seal register. The first board resolution (as set out in the framework) is passed by written consent of the directors and filed in the register of minutes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued)
Approved Memorandum and Articles of Association
Register of Members
Register of Directors and Secretaries
Register of Charges
Written consent of directors adopting the First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any register is incomplete, the Registrar may direct an amendment under section 71 of the Act. The company has 21 days to rectify the defect without penalty; continued non-compliance may trigger a daily penalty of WST 50.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for taxation and business identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Samoa (formerly Samoa Tax Administration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Although a Samoa International Company conducting offshore operations is generally exempt from domestic income tax, the company must obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and, if applicable, register for Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2003. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation and constitutional documents to the Ministry for Revenue. For this stage, only the TIN registration is required; GST registration is deferred until the company begins taxable supplies within Samoa.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (certified copy)
Application for TIN (form IRD-01)
Identification of directors and ultimate beneficial owners
Registered agent declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TIN application is delayed due to incomplete beneficial ownership disclosure, the company may submit a statutory declaration from the registered agent confirming receipt of complete KYC documentation, and the Ministry will issue an interim TIN within 3 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of corporate governance framework and convening of first director meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, Samoa International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a physical or virtual first meeting of the board of directors to formally adopt the First Board Resolution, approve the issue of shares to subscribers, adopt the governance charter, appoint the authorised bank signatories, and delegate the opening of bank accounts. Minutes of the meeting must be recorded in the register of minutes and maintained at the registered office. Any director conflict of interest must be disclosed under section 52 of the Act.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (written consent)
Minutes of the first director meeting
Share certificate for the initial subscriber
Governance charter and conflicts of interest policy
Appointments of bank signatories and authorised representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect is found in the governance documents, the directors may pass a ratifying resolution. If the defect relates to a statutory filing (e.g., failure to file a notice of change), the late filing fee of WST 100 per document may apply and a corrective filing must be made within 7 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health, Samoa (Regulatory Division, Medicines and Medical Devices Control) acting as the licensing authority for medical device manufacturing, together with the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) for development approval
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing Establishment Licence under the Medicines and Medical Devices Act 2007 and the Medical Devices Regulations 2012, supplemented by the Trade Certificate for Industrial Manufacturing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) within the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Development Consent with Environmental Assessment; a full EIA Report is required only if the facility exceeds 200 square metres or uses hazardous substances. For a thermoforming and trimming facility of dental aligners, a 'Development Consent with Environmental Conditions' is applicable, not a full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with the Water Resources Act 2008 and the Samoa National Water Quality Standards: pH 6.0–8.5, BOD5 not exceeding 20 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, and no visible oil or grease. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from thermoforming must be controlled to a maximum of 50 mg/m³ at the exhaust stack. Plastic off-cuts and rejected aligners must be segregated under the Waste Management Act 2005 and handed to a licensed recycler; no hazardous waste may be disposed of on site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) confirming compliance with the Fire Safety Code 2009, including smoke detection, extinguisher placement, and emergency egress; structural load inspection certificate from the Building Inspectorate, Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) verifying the floor loading capacity for thermoforming machinery; and a Workplace Occupational Health Clearance from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002 confirming safe handling of polymer materials, ventilation of fumes, and provision of personal protective equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Apia, Samoa; official taxpayer portal: SRA Online Services (https://www.sra.gov.ws); entity registry: Samoa International Companies Registry under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC): (1) Appoint a licensed registered agent in Samoa and incorporate the IC under the International Companies Act 1987 via the MCIL Registry; obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Registration of International Company. (2) Submit to the Samoa Revenue Authority the SRA Taxpayer Registration Application (Form T1) attaching the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, register of directors and shareholders, registered office certificate, and passport copies of directors. (3) File a non-resident business declaration confirming the IC will not carry on business in Samoa with Samoan residents and will not derive gross income from sources within Samoa, thereby preserving the statutory tax-exempt regime. (4) The SRA issues a single Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) in electronic form within 5-10 working days; the IC is recorded as 'Non-Resident Tax-Exempt International Company' and no VAGST registration number is issued. (5) If the IC later makes taxable supplies in Samoa or to Samoan residents, the SRA must be notified within 14 days and mandatory VAGST registration applies once annual turnover reaches WST 60,000.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box pass-through election and no OECD hybrid mismatch election under the Income Tax Ordinance 2015. The only statutory election: an International Company may voluntarily file an SRA notice to surrender its tax-exempt status and be treated as a resident company for income tax and VAGST purposes; the election is irrevocable for at least five Samoan tax years and triggers full domestic tax obligations. An IC may also elect to exclude resident ownership or to issue bearer shares per its charter without changing the tax-exempt default. No partnership pass-through classification exists for ICs; entity-level taxation arises only upon a valid resident-election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) — a VAT-model consumption tax under the VAGST Act 2007
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 60,000 (annual taxable turnover of supplies made in Samoa in any 12-month period; a person making only zero-rated exports of goods is nonetheless eligible for voluntary registration; tax-exempt International Companies are outside the charge unless resident-election is made)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa currently imposes no national mandatory real-time e-invoicing, no fiscal data clearance to government APIs, and no digital stamping requirement. The SRA requires every registered taxable person to issue a VAGST tax invoice within 28 days of supply, showing the seller's TIN, VAGST registration number, supply date, description, quantity, tax-exclusive value, and the 15% VAGST amount. Zero-rated export invoices must be clearly annotated 'Zero-Rated Export — VAGST Act 2007, s. 12(1)' and include the overseas buyer's details. Compliance is monitored through periodic SRA desk audits, customs export cross-matching, and VAGST return reconciliation rather than real-time transactional clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods (thermoformed multilayer dental clear-aligner sheets and finished aligners): (i) the IC supplies the goods in the course of its export-oriented business to a buyer who is outside Samoa and not a Samoan resident; (ii) the goods are physically removed from Samoa by the IC or its agent within 28 days after the day of supply, or within any longer period approved by the SRA Commissioner; (iii) the IC retains the complete statutory export evidence bundle; (iv) the goods are not re-imported into Samoa or diverted for local consumption without SRA consent. Offshore services (e.g., aligner design data services, IP licensing to a non-resident distributor): zero-rating applies where the recipient is a non-resident outside Samoa at the time of supply, the services are performed outside Samoa and not for a Samoan permanent establishment, and the benefit is enjoyed wholly outside Samoa; services relating directly to Samoan land or physical personal property in Samoa are ineligible.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SRA Customs Export Declaration (electronic cargo declaration) bearing the approved export entry number and exit stamp of the Samoan Customs post
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the dental-aligner goods from Samoa within the statutory 28-day window
Commercial invoice and underlying purchase order from the overseas buyer, with full buyer identity and offshore delivery address
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a licensed Samoan bank, evidencing credit of export proceeds in foreign currency from the offshore buyer
Certificate of Origin (Form A or non-preferential certificate) where preferential tariff treatment or buyer customs clearance requires it
VAGST export tax invoice annotated 'Zero-Rated Export — VAGST Act 2007, s. 12(1)'
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SRA and Samoan Customs conduct targeted audits of export zero-rating claims, cross-matching export declarations, bills of lading, IRC bank records, and VAGST returns. Where zero-rating is claimed without statutory substantiation: the Commissioner disallows the claim, reassesses the supply at the standard 15% VAGST, and issues an assessment for the tax shortfall plus a late-declaration penalty of 25% of the shortfall and deficit interest at 2% per month compounded from the original due date; the Commissioner may reassess within 7 years from the date of the fraudulent or wilful-default claim. Criminal sanctions under the VAGST Act 2007 and Customs Act 2014: corporate fines up to WST 50,000; directors and officers individually liable to fines up to WST 20,000 and/or imprisonment for a term up to 2 years. Fraudulent export declarations also constitute exchange-control offences under the Exchange Control Act 1972 (failure to repatriate export proceeds within the prescribed period attracts monetary penalties up to the value of the export proceeds) and money-laundering predicate offences under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2018, exposing the IC and its beneficial owners to asset forfeiture and debarment from Samoan licensed banking channels.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a controlled but trade-convertible currency. The CBS administers the Exchange Control Regulations 1976/1983 and enforces a bifurcated regime: current account transactions are generally freely convertible with documentary verification, while capital account transactions require express CBS approval. For a Samoa International Company (IC), profit remittances in the form of dividends, reinvested earnings, and repatriation of liquidation proceeds are conceded as current account transfers once the IC is fully tax-exempt and possesses a CBS-approved tax exemption certificate. In practice, remittances above WST 200,000 equivalent are subjected to a CBS exchange control form with underlying audited financial statements, board resolutions, and evidence of regard for the non-resident beneficial owners. The WST is not an offshore deliverable currency; offshore clearing is limited to NASDAQ-traded WST crosses through tier-1 correspondent banks, with final settlement onshore in WST or an approved foreign currency account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The CBS Exchange Control Policy requires all export proceeds from physical movement of dental clear aligner sheets out of Samoa to be credited to a licensed Samoan bank account within 30 calendar days of payment receipt, or 90 calendar days of shipment if financing is under an open account facility. The mandatory surrender and conversion ratio is 100% of export receipts into WST unless the exporter holds a general or special CBS foreign currency retention exemption. For a Samoa IC with operational foreign currency cash cycles, CBS may grant a standing exemption allowing up to 100% retention in USD/EUR for up to 180 days, with quarterly reconciliation and proof of ongoing intercompany trade.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (Samoa) Limited

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / WST Importer Exporter Account
Operational Account / Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Moderate. Samoa's financial sector perimeter requires any entity holding client funds or executing remittances in Samoa to be licensed or expressly recognized by the CBS. Offshore digital EMIs like Revolut Business or Wise are not standalone licensed in Samoa and may not act as the primary clearing bank for a Samoa IC. They can serve as auxiliary disbursement rails for supplier payments only if the IC maintains a local account at a licensed commercial bank and obtains CBS approval for each outbound transfer exceeding WST 200,000 equivalent. Because dental-aligner sheet production involves raw polymer imports and premium orthodontic returns, reliance on unregulated EMIs is not advisable as the substantial treasury backbone.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted for Samoa International Companies. Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Act 2014 and successive CBS guidelines, licensed banks may perform reliable electronic KYC via notarized ID, passport scans, and live video interview with the signatories. Directors are not required to appear physically at a Samoan bank branch. However, certain tier-1 banks may impose an internal, face-to-face or locally notarized verification step where the beneficial-owner structure contains trusts or foundations. At least one Samoan-registered agent or local authorized representative is generally required for service-of-process and regulatory correspondences. The IC should budget for a 4-to-6 week onboarding period plus a possible interview with the bank's compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque offshore company structure with nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete Schedule of Beneficial Owners, notarized declaration of trust if nominee shareholders are used, CBS-compliant registry excerpt from the Samoa International Companies Office, formal directors' identification, and audited group organizational chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dental clear aligner sheets flagged as dual-use medical device under export control screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC v4 classification certification (3250), NAICS mapping to HS 9018/3920, ISO 13485 medical device quality management certificate, CE/FDA/TGA product registration if applicable, technical datasheet of PETG/polyurethane multilayer sheets, and end-user declarations from licensed orthodontic laboratoires.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual third-party payments or back-to-back letter of credit structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts, intercompany loan agreements, SWIFT MT103/MT202 reference copies, freight documents, bill of lading, packing lists, insurance certificates, and board resolutions approving treasury counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance in Samoa and lack of local business footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing, registered-office lease in Apia, minutes of board meetings held in Samoa, evidence of local administrative staff engagement, Samoan tax-free status certificate, and credible business plan showing real decision-making in the jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the IC's designated Samoa account. The receiving CBS-licensed bank requires the remitter to identify the Samoa IC registration number and mandatory CBS purpose code: 6000 for equity subscription, 6100 for shareholder loan, or 6210 for capital contribution in kind. The bank must verify the source of funds, underlying board approval, and (if the capital injection exceeds WST 200,000 equivalent) complete CBS Form EXC-4 exchange-control approval before final crediting. Proceeds from crowdfunding, crypto, or non-banking channels are not permitted to be deposited into the treasury accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for raw polymer rolls, packaging materials, and aligner softwares are cleared via SWIFT MT103 (direct payment) or MT202 (interbank cover). For larger transactions, Samoa banks issue Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700/MT707) confirmed through ANZ or BSP, or operate documentary collection (DP/DA). The IC must provide Customs Pre-Advice, certificate of origin, invoice, packing list, and proof of prior export proceeds repatriation when tapping into USD/EUR working-capital accounts. Payments to related group entities attract transfer-pricing audit risk; therefore each disbursement should carry a purpose code of 4200 (imports of materials) or 4300 (intra-group services) with a contemporaneous OECD compliant benchmark.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore WST/USD forward contracts with CBS-licensed commercial banks, covered by confirmed export orders
Onshore WST/EUR forward contracts for European resin feedstock purchases
Currency swaps with CBS-registered counterparties where both legs are real commercial obligations
FX call and put options traded through licensed bank treasury desks, collateralized by the IC's onshore deposits
CBS-pre-approved non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where an offshore WST hedge is structurally unavoidable, subject to quarterly usage declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Renewal Fee for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation; renewal window opens 60 days prior and closes on the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% per month on the unpaid fee; continued non-payment for 90 days permits the Registrar to strike the company off the International Companies Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership and Shareholding
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent, acting under the Samoa Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2007 and International Companies Act 1988
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary of incorporation; within 14 days after any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain and confirm beneficial ownership records is an offence under the AML/CFT Act, subject to fines and possible imprisonment of the registered agent and responsible officers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Maintenance Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; confirmation required at annual renewal and within 30 days of any change of registered agent or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent and registered office in Samoa results in suspension of the company's International Company status, loss of tax exemption, and eventual strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit thresholds apply. An Samoa International Company is exempt from statutory audit regardless of revenue, assets, number of members, or public interest status. Audited financial statements are not required to be filed with any government authority.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory accounting framework is imposed by Samoa law. If financial statements are prepared voluntarily, IFRS or US GAAP are commonly used; records may be maintained in any jurisdiction and in any currency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must identify every registered member and every ultimate beneficial owner. At least once per year, and immediately upon any share transfer, the company must provide written confirmation of current shareholding and beneficial ownership; the agent must update the ownership register within 14 days. No public UBO filing is made to the government, but the register is available to Samoa regulatory authorities upon lawful request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required; $0 if unaudited; $2,500 – $6,000 if a voluntary audit is engaged

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for resident companies under the Samoa Income Tax Act 2015; 0% effective rate for a qualifying International Company with no Samoan-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The International Companies Act 1987 grants a comprehensive statutory exemption to a qualifying Samoa International Company: no income tax, no dividend/interest/royalty withholding tax, no capital gains tax, no stamp duty, and no estate duty on non-Samoan-source income. For the dental clear aligner sheet business, offshore manufacturing, IP licensing and international sales income of the IC can enjoy a permanent 0% effective rate provided the IC does not carry on business with Samoa residents and does not derive Samoan-source manufacturing or domestic sales income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return prescribed under the International Companies Act 1987 and filed through the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry, Labour and Immigration online Company Registry e-Services portal by the licensed Samoa registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, based on the anniversary of incorporation; no separate Samoa corporate income tax return is required for a tax-exempt International Company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 30 calendar days after the annual return date, which is the anniversary of incorporation. The annual Registry fee must be paid at the same time or the return is treated as unfiled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IC registration number and company name
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact certificate number and registered English name; non-resident applicants must act through the licensed Samoa registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office in Samoa and registered agent details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A physical Samoa street address maintained by the licensed agent is mandatory; a PO Box or foreign address is rejected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and secretary details: full legal name, nationality, residential address, and occupation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and secretary are allowed; provide full residential address for service of process and disclose any alternate director arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, class of shares, and shareholder register
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all non-resident shareholders and, where applicable, the underlying beneficial owners; bearer shares are not permitted for a compliant filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of international business status and confirmation that no Samoan-source business is transacted
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners should confirm that all dental aligner sheet sales, IP licensing and procurement activities occur outside Samoa; transactions with Samoa residents other than licensed offshore activities must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent certification and electronic signature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The licensed Samoa registered agent must co-sign and certify the filing; electronic signatures through the portal are accepted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed administrative penalty and continuing monthly surcharges as prescribed under the International Companies Act 1987; continued default beyond three months exposes the IC to Registry deregistration, loss of legal standing to enforce contracts, and a further reinstatement fee before the corporate veil can be restored.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends and distributions paid by a Samoa International Company to non-resident shareholders because the IC is tax-exempt and distributions are outside the Samoa income tax system. By contrast, a pure Samoa domestic company paying a dividend to a non-resident would be subject to the domestic dividend withholding tax rate of 15% unless a treaty applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief application is required for a tax-exempt International Company distribution because no Samoa withholding tax arises. Where a payment is nevertheless treated as Samoan-source, the protocol is: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the recipient jurisdiction; (2) submit the prescribed Samoa treaty relief form and beneficial ownership declaration to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before payment; (3) obtain a written treaty rate determination; (4) withhold at the treaty rate, file the withholding reconciliation, and retain the TRC, ownership chain documentation and board resolutions for at least seven years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For a Samoa International Company, payments of IP royalties and debt interest to non-residents are exempt from Samoa withholding tax at 0%. For a domestic Samoa company paying such amounts to a non-resident, the statutory withholding tax rate is 15%, potentially reduced to 0%–10% under an applicable double tax agreement, subject to a valid TRC and beneficial ownership proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory monetary threshold is codified in the Samoa Income Tax Act; however, the Samoa Revenue Authority may demand contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for any cross-border related-party transaction regardless of amount. A prudent Samoa International Company transacting in dental clear aligner sheets or IP royalties with connected parties should prepare OECD-compliant Local File and Master File documentation when annual related-party turnover exceeds WST 5,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Samoa Economic Substance Regulations apply to International Companies carrying on relevant activities, including distribution and service centres, IP holding, financing, leasing, headquarters, shipping, investment funds, banking and insurance. A dental clear aligner IC that licenses intellectual property to contract manufacturers or resells finished aligner sheets through related parties must demonstrate Samoan direction and management, adequate local employees and physical premises, and performance of core income-generating activities in Samoa. An IC limited to passive equity holding of a dental-aligner subsidiary benefits from a reduced substance requirement but must still file the annual economic substance return. Failure to satisfy the tests can trigger monetary penalties, exchange of information to foreign tax authorities, and deregistration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misrepresenting the IC as a pure offshore entity while actually operating a thermoforming production line or selling dental aligner sheets to Samoa residents, or fabricating board minutes and offshore contracts to disguise Samoan-source business income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the income as Samoan-source and taxable at the 25% corporate rate; imposition of unpaid tax, late payment interest, and an evasion penalty of up to 50% of the tax underpaid; prosecution under the Income Tax Act 2015 with criminal fines registrable against the corporate estate and possible deregistration of the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who knowingly authorised false filings can be personally assessed where the corporate veil is pierced; civil restitution of evaded tax, travel bans pending recovery, disqualification from serving as a director, and imprisonment upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining only a brass-plate registered office with no Samoan employees, no local board meeting, no premises, and no locally performed decision-making while deriving revenue from dental aligner IP royalties or back-to-back product resales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory economic substance filing penalties, a direction to amend the IC's business structure, exchange of information with foreign tax authorities, strike-off and deregistration of the IC, and revocation of the IC tax exemption with retroactive assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors jointly liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; directors also face personal financial penalties, travel restrictions, disqualification orders, and civil claims by creditors and revenue authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dental clear aligner sheets to a related distribution entity at an undervalue, or paying artificially inflated royalties to a connected IP company in a zero-tax jurisdiction, using a Samoa IC as an invoice pass-through with no arm's length comparability analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Samoa Revenue Authority may adjust taxable income to the arm's length value, disallow excess deductions, impose a transfer pricing adjustment penalty of 25% of the underpaid tax, and charge interest from the original due date; continued abuse can trigger professional conduct investigations of the Samoan tax agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where transfer pricing manipulation is knowingly directed by board members, those directors are personally liable for the corporate tax shortfall, loss of the benefit of limited liability, and may be subject to criminal fines, a travel ban, and imprisonment for tax-related fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Hiding the true family trust settlor or discretionary beneficiary of the Samoa IC, failing to maintain a beneficial ownership register, or routing dental aligner patient payments through Stripe and credit card platforms in a manner that cannot be reconciled with disclosed legal ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil and criminal penalties under the Samoa Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2007, including fines up to WST 200,000 for the IC and suspension of the licensed Samoan registered agent; the IC may be deregistered and reported to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and trustees can be made personally liable for money laundering offences, with asset forfeiture, court-ordered travel bans, surrender of passports, and imprisonment up to 14 years; the corporate veil is set aside where a company is used as an instrument of concealment.
